chapitres.competenceChapitre: Exploring medical innovations, traditional remedies, and making informed health choices. Developing reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills related to healthcare topics.

objectifsLesson.description: Read a text about a medical invention (e.g., the Cardio pad) to identify its purpose, function, and implementation challenges.
Vocabulary: Medical technology, innovation (e.g., device, examination, specialist, interpret, effective).
Grammar: Using the passive voice to describe processes and inventions ('The Cardio pad was invented by Arthur Zang.').
Listen to a discussion or interview comparing modern, traditional, and alternative medicine to identify the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Vocabulary: Healthcare systems (e.g., modern medicine, traditional medicine, alternative medicine, chronic disease, treatment).
Grammar: Using comparative and superlative forms to evaluate options ('Modern medicine is often more precise, but traditional medicine can be more accessible.').
Engage in a debate or role-play where a patient and a doctor discuss the pros and cons of different treatment options, using persuasive language.
Vocabulary: Persuasion and advice (e.g., recommend, advise, option, effective, risk).
Grammar: Using modals for advice and suggestion (should, could, might).
Write a short essay or an article describing a health problem (e.g., a disease outbreak) and suggesting prevention measures and treatments.
Vocabulary: Disease prevention (e.g., outbreak, transmission, symptoms, prevention, hygiene).
Grammar: Using conditionals (Type 1) to talk about real possibilities ('If you wash your hands regularly, you reduce the risk of infection.').

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Analyzing the impact of scientific and technological advancements on daily life and communication. Developing critical thinking and formal writing skills.

lessons.titreLesson: Session 5 (Reading): The Digital World and its Risks

objectifsLesson.description: Read a text about cybercrime (e.g., phishing, hacking) to understand the methods used by criminals and the consequences for individuals.
Vocabulary: Cybersecurity (e.g., hackers, phisher, personal information, account, fraudulent).
Grammar: Using relative pronouns (who, which, whose) to define and describe technical concepts.

lessons.titreLesson: Session 6 (Listening): The Role of Social Media

objectifsLesson.description: Listen to people discussing the benefits and drawbacks of social media platforms and understand their different viewpoints.
Vocabulary: Social media (e.g., applications, social media, network, platform).
Grammar: Using gerunds as subjects and objects ('Using social media can be time-consuming.').
Discuss how technology has changed communication, work, and leisure, expressing opinions on whether these changes are positive or negative.
Vocabulary: Technology and lifestyle (e.g., smartphones, communication, online, network service).
Grammar: Using the present perfect continuous to talk about ongoing situations ('People have been using smartphones for communication for years.').
Write a formal letter or email to a company (e.g., an internet service provider or electricity company) to complain about a service disruption and its effects.
Vocabulary: Formal correspondence (e.g., complaint, power cuts, disruption, service, frequency).
Grammar: Using formal linking words (therefore, however, consequently).

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Examining environmental challenges like climate change and waste management, and exploring sustainable solutions. Developing advocacy and solution-oriented communication.

objectifsLesson.description: Read a text about the impact of climate change on farming (e.g., unpredictable seasons, crop failure) and identify the causes and consequences.
Vocabulary: Climate and agriculture (e.g., climate change, seasons, rainfall, crops, drought).
Grammar: Using the future continuous to make predictions ('The rainy season will be getting shorter.').
Listen to a documentary or talk about sustainable practices (e.g., recycling, renewable energy) and understand the main arguments.
Vocabulary: Conservation (e.g., recycle, waste, renewable, conserve, sustainable).
Grammar: Using the causative have (get) to talk about services ('We should have our waste collected regularly.').
Brainstorm and discuss practical solutions for environmental problems at the local level (e.g., waste management, water conservation) and present them to the class.
Vocabulary: Action and solutions (e.g., solution, propose, initiative, impact, reduce).
Grammar: Using modals of obligation and necessity (must, have to, need to).
Write an article for a school magazine or local newsletter to raise awareness about an environmental issue and suggest actions to address it.
Vocabulary: Advocacy (e.g., awareness, campaign, protect, preserve, challenge).
Grammar: Using imperatives for giving instructions and calls to action ('Reduce, reuse, recycle.').

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Exploring the value of volunteering, civic responsibility, and addressing social issues. Developing persuasive speaking and writing for social impact.

objectifsLesson.description: Read a text or a dialogue about the personal and community benefits of volunteering (e.g., skill development, self-esteem).
Vocabulary: Volunteering (e.g., volunteer, community service, skills, experience, satisfaction).
Grammar: Using the infinitive of purpose ('He volunteered to help his community.').
Listen to a speech or testimony about a social issue (e.g., gender discrimination, civic rights) and identify the key message and arguments.
Vocabulary: Social justice (e.g., discrimination, rights, equality, justice, freedom).
Grammar: Using reported speech to relay information and arguments ('She said that gender discrimination is not good.').
Prepare and deliver a short persuasive speech to address a school or community issue (e.g., drug use, violence, lack of facilities).
Vocabulary: Persuasion (e.g., I urge you, let us, we must, together, future).
Grammar: Using rhetorical questions for effect ('What kind of future do we want for ourselves?').
Write a speech to be delivered at a fundraising event, explaining the purpose of the project, its importance, and how the funds will be used.
Vocabulary: Fundraising (e.g., funds, raise money, project, support, contribute).
Grammar: Using future tenses (will, going to) to express intentions and promises.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Discussing the link between education, skills, and career opportunities in a changing world. Developing professional communication for job applications and interviews.

objectifsLesson.description: Read an article or essay discussing different paths to employment (e.g., university vs. vocational training, volunteering) and compare the arguments.
Vocabulary: Education and career (e.g., education, training, experience, skills, career, job interview).
Grammar: Using the second conditional to discuss hypothetical situations ('If I passed my Baccalaureat, I would go abroad.').
Listen to a job interview and identify the key questions asked, the candidate's responses, and the reasons for their success or failure.
Vocabulary: Job application (e.g., interview, position, qualifications, salary, applicant).
Grammar: Using the present perfect to talk about life experiences ('I have applied for several jobs.').
Participate in a mock job interview, practicing how to introduce oneself, discuss one's strengths, and answer questions professionally.
Vocabulary: Personal qualities (e.g., hard-working, motivated, skilled, experienced, qualified).
Grammar: Using polite forms (could, would) to ask and answer questions.
Write a formal cover letter in response to a job advertisement, highlighting relevant skills, experience, and motivation.
Vocabulary: Formal letter writing (e.g., I am writing to apply, I am interested in, I believe I am a suitable candidate).
Grammar: Using appropriate tenses and formal structures for a professional context.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Showcasing African innovation, cultural diversity, and the realities of modern African life. Developing descriptive and analytical writing about inspiring figures.

objectifsLesson.description: Read profiles of young African innovators (e.g., Arthur Zang) and texts about modern African solutions to local problems.
Vocabulary: Innovation and progress (e.g., inventor, device, technology, solution, development).
Grammar: Using the simple past to narrate past achievements ('He invented a device that helps heart examinations.').
Listen to contemporary African music (e.g., Afrobeats), podcasts, or interviews to understand modern cultural expressions, social commentary, and aspirations.
Vocabulary: Culture and identity (e.g., cultural diversity, multilingual, identity, tradition, modern).
Grammar: Using the simple present to express general truths and cultural facts ('Cameroonians are multilingual.').
Discuss common perceptions of Africa and contrast them with contemporary realities (technology, entrepreneurship, culture) in a group discussion.
Vocabulary: Perception and reality (e.g., stereotype, reality, development, progress, potential).
Grammar: Using expressions of contrast (although, however, but, on the other hand).

lessons.titreLesson: Session 24 (Writing): A Profile of an Inspiring Figure

objectifsLesson.description: Write a short essay profiling an inspiring contemporary African personality (e.g., an innovator, artist, or leader) and explaining their impact.
Vocabulary: Descriptive writing (e.g., inspiring, influential, leader, role model, impact).
Grammar: Using a variety of sentence structures to create a coherent and engaging profile.
